11.text: This is Lesson 11 of Western Armenian. Listen to this conversation. Aram and Sona are friends, and they're deciding where to eat.

11.meaning: Sona, do you want to eat together?

11.translit: Voch, heru ché. Mod é. Hon, tsakh.
11.armenian: Ոչ, հեռու չէ։ Մօտ է։ Հոն, ձախ։
11.meaning: No, it's not far. It's close. There, on the left.

11.text: Aram asked Sona if she wanted to eat together. Listen.
Repeat each part after him, starting from the end.
Ask your friend, "Do you want to eat together?"
Now ask, "Do you want to drink together?"
Sona asked "Where?" How do you say "Where?"
Do you remember how to say "here"?
To say "near here," Armenian puts "here" first: "here near." Listen and repeat.
Sona asked, "Isn't it far?" The word for "far" is…
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Tell her, "No, it's not far. It's close."
Aram told Sona where the restaurant was: "There, on the left." You know "there." Say it.
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
You know how to say "the Ararat restaurant." Say it.
Tell her, "It's close, on the left."
She asks you again. Answer, "There, on the right."
Sona asked, "How much is it?" Listen.
You've heard "kani" before, in "zhame kaniin," "at what time?" "Kani" means "how much" or "how many." Repeat each part.
Aram said, "Ten dollars." The word for "ten" is…
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Armenian doesn't add an "s" after a number. Say, "ten dollars."
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Ask your friend, "Do you have money?"
Ask your friend, "How much money do you have?"
In earlier lessons you learned to speak politely, the way you'd talk to an elder, a stranger, or a group. With a friend, Armenians talk more casually. Listen to how you ask a friend "How are you?"
Ask your friend, "What do you want to eat?"
You learned "Esek," "Tell me," the polite way. To a friend, you say…
Say to your friend, "Tell me, how much is it?"
You know how to ask "At what time?" Ask it.
Here's how to say "we will eat."
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Ask Sona, "At what time will we eat together?"
Ask her, "Do you want to eat with me at eight?"
Tell her, "The Ararat restaurant. It's close."
Ask your friend, "Do you want to drink something together?"
Say, "It's not far. It's on the right."
Listen to the conversation from the start of the lesson one more time. This time, you'll understand every word.
This is the end of Lesson 11.

12.text: This is Lesson 12 of Western Armenian. Listen to this conversation. Aram and Sona are at a café.

12.meaning: Sona, what do you want to drink?
Two coffees, please. How much is it?

12.translit: Voch, sugh ché. Hos amen pan sugh é.
12.armenian: Ոչ, սուղ չէ։ Հոս ամէն բան սուղ է։
12.meaning: No, it's not expensive. Everything here is expensive.

12.text: Aram asked Sona what she wanted to drink. Ask your friend, "What do you want to drink?"
Sona wanted coffee. The word for "coffee" is…
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Say, "I want a coffee." Remember "a" or "one" comes after the word: "coffee a."
Now ask your friend, "Do you want a coffee?"
Aram said he wanted coffee too. "Too" or "also" is…
Your friend says she wants to eat. Tell her, "Me too."
Aram ordered two coffees. You know "two." Say it.
Say, "two coffees." Armenian doesn't add an "s" after a number.
To be polite when you order, you add "please."
Repeat each part, starting from the end.

12.part: Part 3 — Numbers from ten to twenty

12.text: Armenian builds eleven to nineteen from "ten" plus the number. Eleven is "ten-one."

12.part: Part 3 — Numbers from ten to twenty

12.text: Aram thought twelve dollars was a lot. He said, "It's very expensive." "Expensive" is…
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
You know "very" from "shad lav," "very good." Say, "It's very expensive."
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Tell your friend, "No, it's very expensive. Twenty dollars."

12.translit: Voch, shad sugh é. Ksan dolar.
12.armenian: Ոչ, շատ սուղ է։ Քսան տոլար։

12.text: Sona said everything here is expensive. "Everything" is…
You know "pan" from "pan me," "something." Say, "Everything is expensive."
Ask your friend, "Do you want to eat together?"
Tell her, "Yes, but later." Use "hedo" for "later."
Tell him, "No, it's close. There, on the right."
Ask your friend, "Coffee or wine?" Use "te" for "or" in a question.
Listen to the conversation from the start of the lesson one more time.
This is the end of Lesson 12.

13.text: This is Lesson 13 of Western Armenian. Listen to this conversation. Aram meets Sona in the street.

13.meaning: Hi Sona. Where are you going?

13.translit: Ararad jasharane gertam. Hedes ge kas?
13.armenian: Արարատ ճաշարանը կ'երթամ։ Հետս կու գա՞ս։
13.meaning: I'm going to the Ararat restaurant. Will you come with me?

13.text: Aram asked Sona where she was going. Listen.
"You're going," to a friend, is…
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Ask your friend, "Where are you going?"
"I'm going" is…
Repeat.
Sona said, "I'm going home." "Home" is…
Repeat.
In Armenian you just say "home I'm going." Say, "I'm going home."
Tell your friend, "I'm going to the Ararat restaurant."
Ask your friend, "Are you going home?"
Answer, "No, not me."
Aram asked Sona to come with him. You know "with me." Say it.
"You come," or "you'll come," to a friend, is…
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Ask your friend, "Will you come with me?"
Answer, "Yes, I'll come." "I'll come" is "ge kam."
Repeat "I'll come."
Ask your friend, "Will you come together?"
Answer, "Yes, but later."
Sona asked, "Tonight?" "Tonight" is…
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
"Ays" means "this," and "kisher" means "night." Ask, "Tonight?"
Answer, "Yes, tonight, at eight."
Ask your friend, "Do you want to eat together tonight?"
Answer, "Not tonight. Tomorrow." You know "tomorrow."
Ask, "Tomorrow at what time?"
Answer, "At nine."
Sona asked where the restaurant was. Ask, "Where's the restaurant?"
Aram said, "You go straight, then left." "Straight" is…
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Say, "You go straight."
You know "hedo" means "later." It also means "then," as in "and then." Say, "Straight, then left."
Now say, "You go straight, then right."
Your friend asks if the restaurant is far. Tell her, "No, it's close. Straight, then left."

13.translit: Voch, mod é. Shidag, hedo tsakh.
13.armenian: Ոչ, մօտ է։ Շիտակ, յետոյ ձախ։

13.text: At the end, Sona said, "Let's go!"
Repeat each part, starting from the end.
Say, "Let's go together."
Say, "Let's go home."
Say, "Okay, let's go."
Ask your friend, "How much is a coffee?"
Answer, "Fifteen dollars."
Say, "That's very expensive!"
Ask, "Where are you going?"
Answer, "I'm going home. Will you come with me?"
Answer, "Yes. Let's go together."
Listen to the conversation from the start of the lesson one more time.
This is the end of Lesson 13.
